## Goal

Hosts in Rust integrate without touching Mostra, and every host can prove its integration with a kit.

## Owned requirements

Close each with the check below, through the real public interface (README §3).

| ID | Requirement | Route | Concrete check |
|---|---|---|---|
| HO-01 | Ports for identity, drafts, submissions, reviews, events, addressing, trusted controls and capture, with built-in standalone adapters | M, C | Every port exercised with and without host registration (conformance) |
| HO-03 | A Rust host crate (wire types, client, runtime-bundle management, port traits) | C, X | Rust crate: wire-type snapshot test, client integration against a real instance, spawn and attach, bundle cache; external: crates.io release |
| HO-05 | A host conformance kit with scenarios (durability across restart, exactly-once-in-effect delivery, outbox replay, identity, addressing, trusted-control round trip, hygiene rejections, version negotiation) and expected-failure baselines | C | Conformance kit passes on standalone adapters and both reference hosts; broken host fails expected scenarios; baselines work |
| HO-06 | **Invariant.** No host-specific code in the core; every Jcode need in JCODE_HOST.md is met through generic ports | C, R | Audit: no host-specific identifiers in core packages; every JCODE_HOST row maps to a conformance scenario; Mirza reviews |
| HO-08 | Hosts configure where artifact sources, versions and interaction data live; artifacts, versions and submissions stay readable after the directory the artifact was authored in is removed | I, C | Conformance: host-chosen home; authoring directory removed; artifacts, versions and submissions still readable |

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

- typify wire types from the draft-07 schema with a snapshot test, and a hand-written tokio client;
- spawn and attach;
- bundle management;
- port traits;
- `@mostra/conformance` with scenarios: durability across restart, exactly-once-in-effect delivery, outbox replay, identity, addressing, trusted-control round trip, hygiene rejections, version negotiation, long-lived state, removal of the authoring directory;
- expected-failure baselines;
- a reference test host in Rust and one in TypeScript.

Design detail for this package:

- From WP-06 (D101): conformance scenarios for IN-06 (drafts arrive only through `port/drafts.mirror`, labelled `kind: "draft"`), IN-07 (each policy), IN-08 (filtered subscribe, ack, resume after restart), IN-09 (signals as `signal.raised`, nothing woken by Mostra), IN-10 (wait level and edge, timeout cursors), IN-12 (host down, ordered replay, redelivery with the same `deliveryId`) and LL-02 (policy `none`), against WP-06's real methods.
- typify wire types from the draft-07 schema, committed with a snapshot test; hand-written tokio client; spawn and attach; bundle cache; port traits.
- `@mostra/conformance`: scenarios listed in the WP summary plus one per JCODE_HOST row; expected-failure baselines; reference hosts in Rust and TypeScript.
- Audit for host-specific code in the core.

## Out of scope

- Jcode's own adapter (C03-B)

## Acceptance evidence

- the kit passes against the standalone adapters and both reference hosts;
- a deliberately broken host fails the right scenarios;
- a grep and dependency audit shows no host-specific code in the core;
- every H-01 to H-16 row exercised by a scenario.

Also: `pnpm check` green, diff reviewed, the progress report's evidence table complete for every owned requirement (README §3), the evidence matrix regenerated, docs and AGENTS.md current, and the report finalized after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- typify is Draft-7-centric: keep the schema inside the subset it handles and fail CI when a schema leaves it.

## Handoff

C03-B has everything except tailnet sharing and the Skill, which WP-13 and WP-14 add.
